en: Abhidhānottaratantra, Chapter 18 [Tibetan and Sanskrit, 21] = Lokesh Chandra facsimile edition = 1138 AD palm-leaf manuscript.
Now I shall further explain another method of *Pratyaṅgirā*;
these protections, hidden within other tantras, are extremely difficult to obtain.
These have been taught here in the tantras, each subsequent one surpassing the previous;
one should not entertain doubt for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.
One should draw an eight-petaled lotus, filled with a pericarp and filaments;
outside of that, one should place a double-vajra (viśvavajra) conjoined with the mantra of Sumbha;
outside of that, one should provide boundary lines (mekhalā) and draw sixteen petals.
One should place the *kalā* there and surround it on the outside.
The wise one should draw a twelve-pointed vajra upon the pericarp;
having placed the terrifying and formidable syllable *HŪṂ* right there in the center (*varaṭaka*).
One should write the name of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*) interspersed with the three syllables: *oṃ* at the sound of *hūṃ*, and *vaṃ* in the belly.
There, one should place four *ḍākinīs* in counter-clockwise order.
Ḍāṃ lāṃ khaṃ rūṃ. Then one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*).
One should place Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ along with Ḍākinī. One should place [the seed-syllables] interspersed with the name upon the petals, according to the sequence of the wheel of wisdom (*dhīmat-cakra*).
*Khaṃ* and *praṃ* on the eastern petal; *kaṃ* and *ñcaṃ* on the northern; *kam* and *praṃ* on the western.
In the south is *viṃ* and *sraṃ*. From the southeast (*āgneya*) up to the northeast (*aiśāna*),
[the syllables are] *saṃ*, *vīṃ*, *aṃ*, *khaṃ*, *vaṃ*, *laṃ*, *caṃ*, and *hūṃ*.
Thus, one should draw the heroes, interspersed with the syllable *hūṃ*, in their proper order.
One should draw *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ cchaṃ jaṃ* upon the girdle of the lotus petals.
One should encircle the vajra with twelve vases,
adorned with dots and circles;
outside the sixteen petals, one should draw a sixteen-spoked wheel.
In that very place, one should arrange the Ḍākinīs and Vīras in counter-clockwise order starting from the east:
aṃ eṃ vaṃ māṃ mam; baṃ muṃ; suṃ syāṃ vaṃ maṃ; maṃ haṃ; viṃ khaṃ; maṃ raṃ; raṃ khaṃ; haṃ soṃ; aṃ caṃ; heṃ snaṃ; paṃ maṃ; veṃ caṃ; vaṃ muṃ.

Thus, one should write it interspersed with the syllable *hrīḥ* and interspersed with the syllable *oṃ*. Having enclosed the name of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*) within, one should write it according to the specific ritual requirement:
*jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ [ṇaṃ] taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ*.
One should draw the outer girdle.
Outside the wheel, one should draw a square, and inside, one should draw [the inner square] resting upon the doors.
One should place the seed-syllables of Kākāsyā and the others, up to Yamamathanī, in their proper sequence.
One should interweave the names, joined with the syllables *kaṃ* [78], *druṃ*, *svāṃ*, *sūṃ*, *yaṃ yaṃ yaṃ yaṃ ya*, *ra*, *la*, *va*, *śa*, *ṣa*, *sa*, and *ha*,
and interspersed with the syllable *oṃ haṃ*. One should thus interweave the names.
Above the door, one should draw four lines and a half-moon;
in the corners, one should draw a moon, a sun, and a half-vajra.
Above that, one should visualize the face of an angry deity endowed with eight feet.
On the outside, however, one should write this Pratyāṅgirā in the middle of the girdle.

Homage to all Herukas of body, speech, and mind! Oṃ hūṃ! O Vajra-Heruka-Cakravartin, whatever mechanical devices, mantras, tantras, root-practices, and so forth have been performed by anyone—whether mundane or supramundane—all of them: draw them in! draw them in! threaten them! threaten them! seize them! seize them! devour them! devour them! destroy them! destroy them! strike them! strike them! burn them! burn them! cook them! cook them! crush them! crush them! churn them! churn them! shatter them! shatter them! grind them into a hundred thousand pieces! Oṃ phaṭ!
Vajraherukoṣṇīṣacakravartin, you whose face is the fourth [face], HŪṂ HŪṂ! Grant peace to [name]! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
Having encircled it with this [syllable], one should place it in the center of the interior of the syllable *kṣa*.
Having encircled the exterior of the syllable *kṣa* with the syllable *ṭha*, one should encircle it with the characteristics of the vowels.
Having made oneself the nature of Heruka by means of the seven-syllable mantra, one should recite it.
Oṃ hrīḥ ha ha, bring peace to [name], hūṃ 2! Phaṭ to all sins! Taking *svayambhū* flowers—or those of a *ḍombī*, a Brahmin woman, or especially a princess—mixed with royal flowers;
Having taken up the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), one should mix it with realgar and saffron,
combined with great collyrium, and likewise draw the divine Vajradhara, well-encircled by a garland of vajras, emerging from the lotus-vajra.
Either on human skin, or on birch bark, or on a rag from a corpse;
Having placed [the image] in ghee and milk, one who is firm in his vows should likewise worship it with the mantra consisting of eight words, accompanied by the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). Then,
with golden and silver jars filled with the water of the five nectars of wisdom, [one should worship] the Sun.
One should place the wheel in the center, encircled by a white thread.
Then, having recited the *mālā-mantra*, one should cause the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) to be given.
One should make the innate (*sahaja*) free from affliction (*niruja*), and likewise make the state free from affliction innate.
The wise one should place [the thread] among fish, wine, and liquor;
there, according to the specific ritual procedure, he should make it free from pain and endowed with splendor.
Whatever rite he performs, [it succeeds when the thread] is well-wrapped with the garland-mantra.
The yogin should hold the wheel, which is concealed within the centers of the head;
it certainly brings about the empowerment of the ḍākinīs' mantras, and not otherwise.
One attains the true vehicle and will certainly achieve success without obstacles.
In the *Abhidhānottara*, the eighteenth chapter on *Pratyaṅgirā*. [Colophon]
[ 88 end of folio]
